style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Editorial cut-paper collage arranged on a warm oak study desk, wide 16:9 framing. Split-screen diptych divided by a clean torn-paper seam: left half, a crisp cut-paper residence permit card in cream rag stock with a small rust-red price tag on a string, sharp die-cut edges; right half, a hand-torn wall calendar of blank graphite day squares, one square ripped away leaving ragged fibre. Halftone newsprint texture on every layer, physical cast shadows under each sheet, one raking light from the left, muted palette of bone white, graphite and rust red, generous negative space, no lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, legible numbers, watermark
rationale: A pure policy dilemma with no facility, machine or supply chain is the catalogue's stated case for cut-paper collage. The split-screen diptych stages the article's own section heading — 'priced permit, unpriced test' — as two paper artefacts: one die-cut clean and tagged with a price, the other torn, blank and unfinished. Raking light and real cast shadows on an oak desk keep the abstraction tactile and editorial rather than flat graphic.
subject: a cut-paper residence permit card with a price tag beside a torn wall-calendar grid of day squares
core_thesis: Türkiye's $150,000 investor residence permit prices only legal presence — the tax-residency question stays unbought, because it is settled by day-counting machinery no permit can purchase.
core_conflict: a residence permit with a clean quoted price versus the unpriced, unwritten tax-residency test — 183 weighted days, UK statutory tests, Ireland's 280 days — that ignores the permit entirely.
composition: Split-screen diptych: left half the crisp priced permit card, right half the torn day-count calendar, divided by a clean torn-paper seam, both off-centre with generous negative space
